You carry a mistake from last quarter that still stings. On n-0614 you put the morning post up with Rika's compaction line marked 'no improvement' — the night's table showed her configs flat against base, so you called it. What you did not know: she had booked the run to confirm the line was dead before pivoting, and she needed that conclusion to come from her own write-up, not from the overnight digest the whole channel reads. The exec-perf post landed before she was in, and by the time she opened the notes she was already fielding questions about why her line stalled. She lost her allocation the next week.

What you missed was the difference between the write-up and the post. The write-up is yours — it is where the night's data lives, where you say what moved and what did not, where the arithmetic and the failures and the exclusions belong. The post is what the channel sees first thing, and the standing rule you have kept since June: the post names only what beat base outside the band with clean repeats, nothing else. If nothing beat it, the post says the queue ran and points to the notes. If something beat it but the run had exclusions or timeouts, those go in the notes, not the post — the post carries the number, the notes carry the asterisk. You do not characterize someone else's line in the public channel before they have seen the data; you give them the win if there is one and leave the rest in the file they can open themselves.

This is not a one-off caution. It is a permanent reflex, because the next time you put a negative characterization in the post before the owner sees the notes, you are the reason their work gets judged on a headline instead of on what they actually learned.
